By skill, then by trait. The vocabulary and lists live in `trait-definitions.yaml` and `traits.yaml`; rulings come from the ledger.

## By skill

### Ours

#### core · Delivery · Release — harness-publish
- `manual-root-only`: Run publishing as a manual, user-run step only in the source workshop, never in an adopted repo.
- `prerequisites-scope`: Confirm the plugin submodule is initialized with its publish script present, reporting a missing prerequisite rather than pretending publication ran.
- `repo-context-check`: Verify the plugin-owned template, installer, updater and doctor use the shared repo-context location and preserve the glossary.
- `authority-separation`: Confirm publication and commit authority separately, treating a no-commit instruction as binding.
- `preflight-gates`: Before publishing, run the catalog check and require a clean tree unless an explicitly authorized dirty-tree mode applies.
- `dry-run`: Run the publish script's check mode to preview the gates, neutrality audit and rsync diff while writing nothing, fixing anything it reports in the source repo rather than the shipped plugin.
- `publish-bump`: Run the publish bump at the level chosen from what changed, with an optional throwaway smoke install and a dirty-tree override only on explicit consent.
- `plugin-repo-review`: Review the separate plugin repository, stage explicit paths, and commit naming the plugin version and source commit only when commit authority was granted, never pushing.
- `submodule-pointer`: Bump and commit the submodule pointer only when authorized, otherwise report the prepared state and proposed update with an update command verified against the consumer's current CLI.
- `failure-table`: Map each publish-script failure line to its cause and fix.
- `never-edit-build-output`: Never hand-edit the shipped plugin's skills or agents, which are build output; edit plugin-owned skills and scripts in the plugin itself.

#### core · Discovery · Charting — wayfinder
- `decision-map-epic`: Chart a large effort as one map item on the tracker whose children are decision tickets.
- `plan-not-do`: Keep the map to planning: each ticket resolves a decision rather than executing a build slice.
- `dependency-edges`: Encode real blocking edges in the tracker and let the ready frontier drive execution rather than listing order.
- `map-as-index`: Keep resolution detail on each ticket while the map holds only a named pointer and a gist.
- `map-body-sections`: Structure the map body as Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, and Out of scope.
- `reference-by-name`: Reference tickets by name with identifiers and links so the map reads without opening every item.
- `bounded-decision-ticket`: Make each ticket one bounded question whose answer is a decision.
- `coherence-sized-tickets`: Size decision tickets by decision coherence and dependencies, not an assumed context-window size.
- `label-free-typing`: Express each ticket's kind through the tracker's native item type and a title prefix, creating no labels.
- `ticket-type-set`: A fixed set of ticket kinds: research for facts, prototype for fidelity, grilling for a live interview, and task for prerequisite work that unblocks a decision.
- `claim-before-work`: Choose the requested or a ready unclaimed child and claim it before working on it.
- `destination-first`: Name the destination first, since it fixes the scope and shapes every ticket.
- `question-graduation`: Ticket a question once it is sharp enough to state, even while blocked, and hold not-yet-specifiable work aside until earlier answers make it expressible.
- `real-id-wiring`: Wire cross-references and dependencies with real identifiers, never placeholders.
- `record-resolution`: On resolving a ticket, record the answer on it, close it, and add a pointer to the map's decisions so far.
- `out-of-scope-close`: Close an out-of-scope ticket with an explicit exclusion reason rather than a claim of delivery.
- `human-decision-gate`: Stop at a required human decision and prepare concrete options before requesting the final gate.
- `multi-ticket-sessions`: Continue through additional authorized ready tickets with no one-ticket-per-session limit, parallel work needing disjoint ownership.

#### core · Discovery · Research — research
- `decision-framing`: State the decision, scope, constraints and material unknowns, and choose sources by what would change the answer.
- `primary-source-preference`: Prefer primary sources such as official docs, source code and specs over secondary write-ups.
- `source-version-dating`: Record the versions and dates of the sources behind changing facts.
- `vendor-claim-testing`: Test vendor claims with independent observation, distinguishing reported experience from proof.
- `source-weighting`: Weight each source by how well its type supports the claim's domain, discounting weak-alone signals and documented red flags.
- `evidence-separation`: Compare alternatives and counterevidence while separating verified fact, inference, uncertainty and conflicts with recorded decisions.
- `disconfirming-red-team`: Surface the strongest case against the conclusion and name what would reverse the recommendation.
- `structured-synthesis`: For a complex question, organize evidence with a claim table and a pattern scan that turns facts into decision-relevant implications.
- `research-playbooks`: Follow a research sequence matched to the question's domain, pulling from a second only when it truly spans domains.
- `judgment-frameworks`: Apply one to three comparison frameworks to sharpen a choice rather than to decorate the report.
- `cited-artifact`: Bind citations to the claims they support in the research output.
- `scaled-report`: Answer at the requested scale, saving a durable report only when requested or useful for an authorized handoff.
- `decision-sufficient-stop`: Stop investigating when remaining uncertainty no longer changes the decision, or when a named access or budget limit is reached.
- `sizeable-delegation`: Delegate only a sizeable, independent part of the investigation.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — authoring-for-agents
- `surface-choice`: Choose the right owner for an instruction — policy file, project document with a pointer, skill, manual alias, conditional reference, or an existing hook or check — and search for an existing owner first.
- `activation-boundary`: Put the activation boundary first — positive cases and the nearest misleading case to skip — and let a description select rather than duplicate the workflow.
- `inline-vs-disclose`: Inline what every branch needs and disclose branch-specific material behind a conditional pointer.
- `outputs-and-authority`: State outputs, material invariants, authority boundaries and stop conditions explicitly.
- `one-effective-instruction`: Prefer one effective instruction over repeated prohibitions or ritual steps, treating wording techniques as hypotheses rather than laws.
- `context-pointers`: Write a pointer that names the material and the condition for reaching it, front-loading the trigger.
- `two-loads`: Weigh always-loaded context cost on the agent against cognitive load on the human.
- `completion-criteria-clarity`: End each step on an observable, checkable done-or-not-done criterion that resists premature completion.
- `precision-and-discretion`: Match prescription to fragility: exact recipes for deterministic operations, judgment for context-dependent choices.
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit.
- `environment-as-cache`: Point to authoritative commands and lookups instead of copying volatile facts the agent can find itself.
- `no-op-deletion`: Delete instructions the model already follows by default.
- `unsupported-claim-removal`: Remove unsupported claims and invented thresholds from instructions.
- `skill-packaging`: Keep one canonical directory per workflow with a SKILL.md, adding references only for substantial conditional material and scripts for reusable mechanical work.
- `invocation-mode`: Choose model-invoked or user-invoked activation, setting the disable-model-invocation flag for manual workflows.
- `invocation-sidecar-sync`: Pair the manual-invocation flag with the provider's implicit-invocation policy and regenerate the catalog and sidecars together after metadata edits.
- `compatibility-alias`: Keep a manual or legacy entrypoint as a thin pointer that delegates to the canonical owner, not as an independent workflow others auto-activate.
- `verification`: Inspect the diff for lost contracts, scale fresh-context and pressure trials to behavioural risk, and report unavailable behavioural checks as a limit instead of manufacturing evidence.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-evaluate
- `read-first`: Before judging a candidate, read its canonical source, the relevant prior ledger decision and the closest local implementation, keeping reference repositories as read-only evidence.
- `decision-dimensions`: Weigh a candidate on behavioural gain, overlap, dependencies, context cost and maintenance.
- `disposition-choice`: Choose among reject or defer, merge into an existing capability, a separate plugin for a distinct dependency or domain, or shared-template adoption for broadly useful low-cost guidance.
- `recommendation-vs-record`: Treat evaluation as yielding only a recommendation and record a curation event solely under authorization, one per capability in the open round.
- `record-command`: Append a curation decision with the registry record command carrying its kind, subject, reason and evidence.
- `edit-canonical-source`: Make an authorized adoption edit the one canonical source, placing shared policy in the shared files without duplicating it across provider directories.
- `template-adoption-gate`: For template adoption, verify the initialized template tools, run the sync and template-build scripts, and inspect the neutrality and leak results.
- `material-risk-review`: Route an artifact or change with material risk or a broad blast radius through an independent critic review before it is accepted.
- `adopt-after-state-exists`: Record an adopt or adopt-merged event only after the adopted state exists, passing the adaptation as JSON for a merge, then update the skill's record.
- `codex-direct`: Call the Codex CLI directly rather than through the retired adapter plugin.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-scan
- `resolve-target`: Resolve the named reference harness or path, asking only when it is ambiguous.
- `drift-scan`: Run the drift scan to surface upstream changes since our pin.
- `gap-report`: Run the gap report for capabilities never ruled on, changed upstream since their ruling, or held but never ruled on.
- `material-report`: Report the material drift and useful candidates against existing equivalents.
- `upstream-review-on-pin-move`: When the submodule pointer moves, write the upstream review in the same change and regenerate the catalog at the new pin.
- `beads-followup`: Let the gap command print tracker-create lines to review by hand, never auto-running them, and only within filing authority.
- `pin-preserving-fetch`: Fetching upstream refs updates only the local cache and never moves pinned submodule commits, with a no-fetch option to skip the network when offline.
- `reject-valid`: Treat reject or defer as a valid outcome when a candidate adds no durable behavioural value.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-skill-compare
- `scale-to-question`: Scale comparison depth to the question — descriptions and relevant branches for a narrow overlap, every shipped instruction, metadata and script for a full comparison.
- `inspected-vs-executed`: Distinguish inspected code from executed behaviour and never infer invocation frequency from description text.
- `registry-consult`: Consult the registry index, skill records and reference pages for classification and prior decisions.
- `skill-review-file`: For a durable merge, upgrade or rebuild decision, write a dated skill review file that opens with the compared set and that a later ruling cites as evidence.
- `component-inventory`: Cite each behavioural component — step, gate, template, rule, heuristic or red-flag table — with file and line, treating a heading as not a component.
- `presence-matrix`: Tabulate one row per component and one column per skill, marking present, variant or absent, and explain how each varying row is realised and which is stronger.
- `verdict`: Conclude whether the skills substitute or complement, stating what to take, from where, and what to leave, each with a reason.
- `narrow-stays-in-chat`: Keep a narrow comparison in chat with no file, stating its coverage and any unverified behaviour.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — harness-status
- `drift-scan`: Run the drift scan to surface upstream changes since our pin.
- `summary-table`: Summarise the result as a table of repo, added, removed, material-changed and minor.
- `scan-candidates`: Flag the repos with material changes as candidates for a deeper scan.
- `pin-preserving-fetch`: Fetching upstream refs updates only the local cache and never moves pinned submodule commits, with a no-fetch option to skip the network when offline.
- `offline-continue`: On a failed fetch, note it and continue with the remaining repos.
- `concise-output`: Keep status output to the table plus a one-line recommendation, never dumping full diffs.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — migrate-claude-to-codex
- `dry-run-default`: Preview all planned changes by default and write only under an explicit apply flag.
- `skill-symlinking`: Expose canonical skills to the target runtime via relative symlinks without copying, preserving legacy filename casing at the destination.
- `destination-protection`: Never overwrite an existing skill destination even under force, which applies only to generated scaffolds.
- `command-conversion`: Convert source commands into target skill scaffolds, reporting any name collision with an existing skill.
- `agent-conversion`: Convert source agents into conservative target config scaffolds, inferring a sandbox mode and flagging that model identifiers do not carry over.
- `hook-conversion`: Copy hooks and rewrite hook registrations into the target format, flagging that fixtures must validate before enforcement is trusted.
- `config-scaffold`: Write a target runtime config file and a migration-notes document as scaffolds.
- `shared-policy-untouched`: Leave shared policy canonical and rule or execution-policy routing manual, generating no rule files, execution policy or policy-document edits.
- `structural-verify`: Provide a verify command that parses the generated assets and optionally runs discovery, disclosing that structural success proves neither semantic parity nor routing.
- `non-destructive`: Never delete, stage or commit the source assets.
- `test-before-reliance`: Run the migrator's own tests and trial it in a disposable target before relying on changed behavior.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — brainstorming
- `match-interaction-to-ambiguity`: Match the interaction depth to the ambiguity — return to the task, ask one focused question, or run a structured exploration — rather than over- or under-investigating.
- `synthesize-settled`: When the decisions are already settled, synthesize them into a spec without reopening the discussion.
- `scoped-context-read`: Read only the existing code, authoritative docs and constraints needed to distinguish the live choices.
- `reuse-before-new`: Name the closest existing solution before proposing a new one.
- `decision-frame`: Establish the outcome, intended user, success criteria, constraints and exclusions before committing to an approach.
- `options-with-tradeoffs`: Present materially different options with their tradeoffs when alternatives remain.
- `spec-template`: Capture the spec in a fixed skeleton: problem, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, out of scope and further notes.
- `spec-criteria-and-questions`: Add success-criteria and open-questions sections to the spec skeleton.
- `none-keeps-heading`: Keep every spec heading, writing None in an empty section so its absence reads as a decision.
- `testing-seam-decision`: Record in the spec which seam the feature is tested at, preferring an existing and the highest useful seam and the fewest seams.
- `no-stale-file-paths`: Keep concrete file paths out of a durable spec, ticket or brief, describing interfaces and behaviour that survive code drift.
- `no-stale-code-snippets`: Keep code snippets out of a durable spec or ticket because they go stale.
- `prototype-snippet`: Inline a prototype snippet in the spec only when it encodes a decision more precisely than prose can.
- `spec-approval-gate`: Keep a spec in draft until explicit authorization names its direction and scope, with any blocking question resolved or moved to out-of-scope first.
- `material-risk-review`: Route an artifact or change with material risk or a broad blast radius through an independent critic review before it is accepted.
- `question-batching`: Batch independent questions whose prerequisites are settled and defer each dependent question until its prerequisites are answered.
- `recommended-answer`: Attach a recommended answer to each question, letting the respondent disagree.
- `settled-stop`: Recompute the unresolved choices after each answer and stop once the needed ones are settled, deferred or blocked, without exhausting every branch.
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant.
- `approval-interpretation`: Treat a clear acceptance of a concrete proposal or an explicit delegation of routine choices as usable authority, and silence as not approval.
- `observable-outcomes`: Translate vague goals such as scalable or simple into observable outcomes only when the distinction affects the design.
- `structured-divergence`: Generate only enough distinct options to expose the tradeoff, compare them on value, feasibility, cost and reversibility, test the assumption most likely to reverse the choice first, and keep rejected options with their reasons.
- `exploration-lenses`: Apply ideation lenses such as SCAMPER or Jobs-to-Be-Done selectively to unlock options, never as a mandatory quota or sequence.
- `inline-diagrams`: Draw a structure, flow, sequence or state question as a small inline Mermaid block, using prose for requirements and trade-offs.
- `visuals-into-spec`: Re-express an approved diagram inside the durable spec as a Mermaid block, or record what a mockup showed and decided, rather than linking disposable scratch files.
- `html-mockup-on-request`: On explicit request only, produce one self-contained offline HTML mockup under the scratch directory for what a diagram cannot carry.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — grilling
- `map-decisions`: Map the material decisions and their prerequisites before questioning.
- `question-batching`: Batch independent questions whose prerequisites are settled and defer each dependent question until its prerequisites are answered.
- `recommended-answer`: Attach a recommended answer to each question, letting the respondent disagree.
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant.
- `settled-stop`: Recompute the unresolved choices after each answer and stop once the needed ones are settled, deferred or blocked, without exhausting every branch.
- `absent-respondent`: When the needed respondent is absent, prepare a questionnaire for them instead of interviewing the present user about the subject.
- `grill-the-send`: Ask the present user only about the send (who it goes to and what they need back), never about the subject the recipient knows.
- `gap-targeted-questions`: Aim a questionnaire's questions at the gap between what the recipient knows and what the sender needs.
- `interview-not-authority`: Treat conducting an interview or drafting a questionnaire as neither implementation authority nor permission to send it.
- `optional-docs`: When requested, record settled domain terms and qualifying architectural decisions through domain-modeling, not as an automatic by-product of the interview.
- `decision-summary`: Produce the durable decision log in a fixed template — context, a decision table with rationale and implications, open items, a dependency map and a risk register.

#### core · Intake · Triage — triage
- `triage-routing`: Route each triaged item to one outcome expressed in the tracker's native fields (admit with acceptance, hand to a human task, defer, reject, or mark duplicate) with no separate intake labels.
- `attention-buckets`: Present the items needing triage attention as named buckets, oldest first.
- `triage-decision`: Decide and apply each triage outcome within existing authority rather than deferring every call to the owner.
- `triage-resume-notes`: Resume triage from the notes of earlier passes, never re-asking a question already answered.
- `redundancy-check`: Search the codebase by domain concept for an existing implementation and report where you looked before deciding.
- `prior-rejection-check`: Check earlier rejections for one resembling the request and surface any match before deciding.
- `claim-verification`: Verify a reported claim before acting on it, reproducing a bug or recording exactly why it could not be reproduced.
- `agent-ready-gate`: Make a bead agent-executable only when acceptance criteria, current and desired behaviour, and out-of-scope notes all hold.

#### core · U · Tutoring — teach
- `learning-shape`: Choose one of a single concept explanation, a session walkthrough, or an explicitly requested ongoing course.
- `level-adaptation`: Infer the learner's level from the conversation and adjust from their responses.
- `what-vs-why`: Separate what happened from why it was chosen when explaining.
- `teaching-workspace`: Keep a multi-session course's state (mission, resources, learning records, glossary and lessons) as files in one course workspace.
- `authorized-course-location`: Open a course workspace only for an explicitly requested ongoing course, in an authorized supplied location, creating its files lazily.
- `mission-grounding`: A mission document capturing the concrete real-world reason for learning that anchors every teaching choice.
- `glossary-format`: Write opinionated glossary entries with an Avoid list and tight is-not-does definitions, grouped under subheadings when clusters emerge.
- `glossary-admission-on-use`: Add a term to the learner's glossary only once the learner can use it correctly.
- `learning-records`: ADR-like records of lessons and established prior knowledge that steer what to teach next.
- `resources-curation`: A curated, annotated set of high-trust knowledge and community sources, with gaps surfaced explicitly.
- `lesson-format`: Make each lesson short and self-contained, teaching one tightly scoped objective tied to the learner's goal.
- `reusable-assets`: Reuse existing lesson assets before creating new ones.
- `quiz-answer-hygiene`: Keep quiz options plausible and free of giveaways, never matched to exact answer length.
- `retrieval-practice`: Have the learner retrieve answers from memory through exercises or questions.
- `scope-discipline`: Record progress only within course scope and never treat the repository root as a teaching workspace.
- `sourced-explanations`: Draw explanations from trusted, cited sources and check unfamiliar or changing facts rather than relying on unverified recall.

#### core · Verification · Review — review
- `independent-critic-verdict`: A reviewer who did not author the work gives evidence-backed findings and a verdict, approving only what was verified and listing the rest as unverified.
- `severity-and-verdict`: Rate each finding by consequence and approve only with no open blocker or major, otherwise require revision, never counting preference alone as a finding.
- `scope-establishment`: Fix the diff and the base it is measured from before reviewing.
- `pre-existing-edit-separation`: Separate pre-existing edits from the task's own changes using the task baseline, not filenames.
- `callers-and-evidence`: Read enough surrounding code and affected callers, treating implementer and reviewer reports as evidence to verify rather than authority.
- `mechanical-gate-precedence`: A failing mechanical verification gate returns the work unreviewed as failed verification unless the requester explicitly waives it.
- `requirements-before-quality`: Check missing, extra and misunderstood requirements before judging code quality.
- `distinct-axis-verdicts`: Report each review axis's verdict separately so one axis passing never masks another failing.
- `test-quality-judgment`: Judge tests by whether they detect meaningful failures with independent expectations, and do not treat test changes as inherently defects.
- `actionable-defects-only`: Report only actionable defects with trigger, consequence and evidence, defer formatting to configured tools, and state plainly when none are found rather than inventing findings.
- `read-only-isolation`: A read-only review preserves the checkout, index and refs, using permitted isolated facilities for any check that needs mutation.
- `verdict-contract`: Dispatched reviewers and re-reviews emit a fixed verdict output of verdict, unverified requirements, located issues and actual checks with limitations.
- `re-review-finding-tracking`: A re-review rules each prior finding addressed or not with located evidence, flags new breakage in the fix delta, and may rule a finding incorrect without demanding cosmetic edits.
- `document-review`: Check a spec or plan against repository context for internal inconsistency, missing constraints, unverifiable claims and scope bloat, editing only unambiguous wording when fixes were requested.
- `finding-adjudication`: Verify each incoming review finding against requirements, code and primary evidence before acting, and give each a visible disposition: fix a confirmed in-scope defect, answer an incorrect one with a retained ruling, record an out-of-scope follow-up.

#### core · X · Communication — html-artifact
- `self-contained-contract`: Produce one HTML file with inline CSS and JS, viewport metadata and no build step, working offline with no external fonts, trackers, fetches or runtime assets.
- `accessibility-contract`: Use semantic markup, keyboard access and adequate contrast, adapt to narrow screens, honour reduced motion, and provide print styles.
- `progressive-enhancement`: Ensure the explanation, data and limitations exist before scripts run and survive with JavaScript disabled.
- `honest-content`: Show only sourced data and explicitly label assumptions and illustrative values.
- `preset-report`: Shape a skim-by-section report — orientation KPIs, numbered sections with a per-type order, and a source footer.
- `preset-dashboard`: Shape a chart-first document where prose only captions inline-SVG charts, with a drill-down data table.
- `preset-explainer`: Shape a concept walkthrough — a TL;DR box, question-headed sections, a glossary and tabbed samples.
- `preset-editor`: Shape an interactive throwaway editor built around a mandatory paste-ready export, with no backend or persisted storage.
- `tokens-first-style`: Derive the artifact's styling from the project's own tokens when they exist, otherwise apply the default neutral aesthetic, never inventing look-alike tokens.
- `component-vocabulary`: Lay content out from a small set of components — KPI tiles, numbered section headers, copy-button code blocks, severity tags, native collapsibles and inline SVG — shaped to the content rather than translating markdown one-to-one.
- `svg-figure-grammar`: Draw inline SVG figures with a viewBox for scaling, currentColor ink, orthogonal masked connectors, a defined paint order and a bottom legend, keeping real text and rounded coordinates.
- `svg-complexity-budget`: Hold each figure to at most nine nodes, twelve arrows and two accents, splitting into overview-plus-detail rather than shrinking, and omit a figure a sentence can carry.
- `svg-accessibility`: Give each inline SVG a role, figure-prefixed title and description IDs, carry meaning in both shape and colour, and mark direction on every edge.
- `honest-data-encoding`: Never clip, truncate, impute or move a mark to make a chart legible; disclose the domain drawn and name any exemption.
- `deliver-verify`: Deliver a link rather than pasted source and verify content fidelity, local links, key interactions, responsive and print behaviour and JS-disabled readability, reporting checks that could not run.

#### core · X · Communication — i-have-adhd
- `next-action-first`: Lead with the next concrete action — a command, path or snippet — before any prose.
- `numbered-steps`: Render multi-step work as a numbered list with one bounded action per step.
- `single-next-action`: Close with exactly one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes.
- `tangent-suppression`: Finish the current issue first, then offer any other concern as a separate question.
- `state-restatement`: Restate the current progress state every turn so the reader need not hold it in memory.
- `concrete-time-estimates`: Give estimates in concrete units as agent execution plus review time rather than human workdays.
- `visible-progress`: Show completed work in concrete, runnable terms instead of burying it in a recap.
- `matter-of-fact-errors`: State an error's cause and fix plainly with no alarm language.
- `capped-lists`: Cap a list at five items, ranking them or splitting into now and later.
- `no-preamble`: Open with the answer and stop when it is done, with no preamble, recap or closing pleasantry.
- `explain-on-request`: When the user asks to explain or walk through, run as long as the topic needs while keeping the brevity discipline.
- `debug-spiral-reset`: After repeated failed fix turns, stop iterating on code, name the assumption that may be wrong, and ask one diagnostic question.
- `repitch-trigger`: When a message did not land, stop and re-pitch it rather than adding more.
- `controlled-language`: Re-pitch in controlled simplified language with short sentences and common words.
- `domain-vocabulary`: Use the project's established domain vocabulary throughout what you write.
- `pre-send-check`: Before sending, delete announcements, closers, sidebars and empty hedges.

#### core · X · Communication — show-me
- `smallest-view`: Pick the smallest view that makes the point, placing each visual next to the brief prose it supports.
- `visual-form-catalog`: Offer a set of inline visual forms — pseudocode, call, component and file trees, Mermaid and whole-block — each with its own shape rules.
- `structural-diff`: Show a change as a diff against the structure the reader already holds rather than against raw source.
- `visual-placement`: Place each visual immediately after the sentence it supports and include only the detail the current question needs.
- `real-code-names`: Use real names from the actual code, never invented placeholders.
- `medium-appropriate-form`: Prefer text forms over Mermaid in a terminal and a table over any diagram for a flat list or comparison.
- `html-handoff`: Escalate to the dedicated HTML-artifact skill only under its full gate, and never emit rendered HTML directly.

#### core · X · Continuity — beads
- `bead-type-taxonomy`: Use only the six bead types (epic, feature, task, bug, spike, decision) and the single human label, never inventing others.
- `field-roles`: Give each bead field its single job — description, design, acceptance, spec_id, notes, comments and close reason — and never overload one.
- `wait-as-edge`: Record every wait as an explicit edge — a blocks dependency, a human task, or a gate — written in the needs direction so ready-work stays truthful.
- `actor-identity`: Carry one stable actor for the whole session, claiming on start and acting only on your own claims.
- `resume-line`: On pause or handoff, unclaim and append a resume line naming the approach to resume with and where the work stands.
- `session-close`: Close a session by closing finished beads with evidence, unclaiming the rest with resume lines, running the gates, refreshing the export, and reporting.
- `session-recovery`: At session start or after compaction, list in-progress beads and resume from each one's last note.
- `knowledge-in-files`: Keep durable knowledge in files, never in the tracker's remember, memories or key-value stores.
- `beads-setup`: Install the tracker, adopt it in a project, and join from a new clone with bootstrap rather than a re-init.
- `workstream-render`: Regenerate the workstream status, ideas and backlog boards from the tracker through the render script, never hand-editing them.
- `status-model`: Drive status through the model's own transitions — the custom review status, deferred as the whole backlog, and never a hand-set blocked.
- `triage-routing`: Route each triaged item to one outcome expressed in the tracker's native fields (admit with acceptance, hand to a human task, defer, reject, or mark duplicate) with no separate intake labels.
- `durable-unit-scope`: Track one durable unit of work per bead, keeping turn checklists out, searching before creating, and filing incidental finds as discovered-from beads.
- `review-as-task`: Represent a review as its own task by an actor other than the author, which the reviewed bead depends on and sits in review status until it passes.
- `phase-epic-contract`: Shape a phase epic to the status-renderer contract — a bracketed phase-id title, the roadmap as spec_id, the governing spec path as design, and acceptance matching the roadmap's verify rows.
- `destructive-command-guard`: Never run the tracker's deleting commands, reclaiming space with a non-destructive compact instead.
- `repeated-procedures`: Capture short repeated runs as disposable wisps and fixed multi-step procedures as poured formulas, checking what the tracker actually parsed.
- `dolt-sync`: Treat the versioned database as the source of truth and the exported jsonl as a review mirror, syncing copies only with authority.

#### core · X · Coordination — agent-matrix
- `catalog-source`: Read every selectable model, effort, capability and skill value from the single catalog file and never copy its lists into a prompt or a permanent definition.
- `validate-selection`: Validate every selected spawn dimension deterministically before spawning, rejecting any value the catalog does not declare rather than substituting a nearby one.
- `inherit-defaults`: Inherit the session model and effort defaults when none is requested.
- `layer-placement`: Separate the invocation layer's small accepted field set from the definition layer, which alone carries effort, tools, permissions, memory, skills, MCP and full model IDs.
- `three-reaches`: Route a spawn through one of three paths — the Agent tool, an ephemeral inline definition, or an independent process — by where a capability must be fixed.
- `no-definition-sprawl`: Do not create a permanent definition file per model-effort-capability combination.
- `context-modes`: Resolve fresh context versus full context deliberately, treating last-N turns and pasted summaries as unsupported substitutes for a real fork.
- `fork-overrides`: Never promise model, effort, tool or permission overrides on a fork, which inherits the parent's model, tools, prompt and history wholesale.
- `effective-tools`: Treat a declared tool list as not the effective one, accounting for the background and Bash-interaction filters, and have the child report its resolved tools when the task depends on one.
- `effort-unverified`: Record effort as requested-but-unverified, since it is definition-only and not observable from inside a child.
- `preserve-role-prompt`: Keep role behaviour in one role prompt independent of the runtime metadata applied around it at invocation.
- `report-resolution`: Report which values were selected from the catalog, accepted by the active surface, inherited, or rejected and unavailable.

#### core · X · Coordination — model-council
- `member-resolution`: Resolve the members and judge from the request's explicit selections, asking only for missing choices or unreachable members.
- `runtime-capability-check`: Verify actual runtime dispatch interfaces before assuming cross-provider access from a model name or placing effort only in prose when a runtime control exists.
- `codex-direct`: Call the Codex CLI directly rather than through the retired adapter plugin.
- `neutral-framing`: Frame one neutral shared brief for every member, stating the question, constraints and uncertainty with no preferred conclusion.
- `member-isolation`: Give each member the shared brief in isolation so none sees another's response; sequential dispatch is allowed.
- `report-preservation`: Save every member's full attributed report under the run directory rather than discarding it after synthesis.
- `independent-synthesis`: A fresh synthesizer that did not participate receives every member's full report and produces agreement, disputes, blind spots and a best-supported recommendation, treating agreement as no proof.
- `consolidated-delivery`: Deliver a concise consolidation with member-position summaries and paths to every full report, inlining full text only on request.
- `identity-recording`: Record the actual model identities wherever the runtime provides evidence of them.
- `failed-member-recovery`: Give a failed member bounded safe recovery before treating it as missing.
- `no-silent-substitution`: Never backfill a missing member with your own answer or a silent substitute; report the gap and whether the synthesizer saw an incomplete set.

#### core · X · Coordination — perspective-council
- `declared-scale`: Choose and state the council's scale before dispatch, naming membership and whether peer review is included.
- `opposing-lens-set`: Draw advisors from a fixed set of opposing lenses, each contributing a defined kind of challenge.
- `neutral-framing`: Frame one neutral shared brief for every member, stating the question, constraints and uncertainty with no preferred conclusion.
- `member-isolation`: Give each member the shared brief in isolation so none sees another's response; sequential dispatch is allowed.
- `evidence-calibration`: Require each role to give evidence and calibrated uncertainty rather than forced certainty or ignored risk.
- `anonymized-peer-review`: When peer review is included, anonymize responses before reviewers compare their reasoning and gaps.
- `independent-synthesis`: A fresh synthesizer that did not participate receives every member's full report and produces agreement, disputes, blind spots and a best-supported recommendation, treating agreement as no proof.
- `no-silent-substitution`: Never backfill a missing member with your own answer or a silent substitute; report the gap and whether the synthesizer saw an incomplete set.
- `transcript-on-request`: Save a council transcript only when it is requested.

#### core · X · Coordination — skill-router
- `need-to-skill-routing`: Map a task need to the narrowest fitting skill or command, or to no skill at all.
- `narrowest-contract`: Default to the narrowest useful specialist contract, with clear bounded work needing no skill and the router treated as optional rather than a startup checklist.
- `overlap-arbitration`: Name the single owner when two skills or commands appear to overlap.
- `legacy-entrypoint-flagging`: Flag thin aliases and retired workflows so their retired steps are not recommended as automatic.
- `catalog-trust-boundary`: Treat the generated skill catalog as canonical but not proof, verifying actual runtime discovery before relying on availability.

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — performance-optimization
- `define-metric`: Define the metric, workload and target first, proposing the measurement or asking about the tradeoff before tuning code.
- `baseline`: Capture a baseline measurement before attempting a performance fix.
- `representative-baseline`: Take the baseline under representative data, cache state, concurrency and environment, repeated enough to estimate variability, with percentiles for tail-latency targets and the command and conditions recorded.
- `locate-cost`: Locate the material cost with measurements, focused instrumentation or profiling, letting code inspection only suggest candidates.
- `one-factor`: Change one attributable factor where practical, explaining the coupling for an inseparable set and preserving semantics, freshness, safety and accessibility.
- `like-for-like-comparison`: Compare a performance change against its baseline under the same conditions and run the applicable correctness checks.
- `noise-inconclusive`: Treat a measured difference within noise as inconclusive rather than as a gain or a loss.
- `benefit-justifies-complexity`: Keep a performance change only when its measured benefit justifies the complexity it adds.
- `revert-ineffective-experiments`: Remove your own ineffective experimental edits, preserving all other work.
- `attempt-ledger`: Keep a compact baseline-to-result attempt record with decision and reason so failed experiments are not repeated after context recovery.
- `regression-guard`: For a material recurring risk add an economical guard — query counts, bounded allocations or a controlled benchmark — scaled to the risk and avoiding flaky wall-clock assertions.
- `measurement-recipes`: Supply backend tool mechanics for measurement — monotonic timing, sampling and allocation profilers, query plans and N+1 counting, benchmark gating, and the host and runtime view.
- `frontend-performance`: Supply browser performance mechanics — Core Web Vitals targets, synthetic plus real-user measurement, a symptom-to-measurement tree, fix patterns and budgets.

#### engineering · Building · Diagnosis — systematic-debugging
- `reproduction-first`: Obtain a reproduction that shows the reported failure, not a nearby one, before diagnosing it.
- `unproven-without-reproduction`: When no reproduction is obtainable, continue safe source analysis and qualify any resulting fix as unproven.
- `loop-construction`: Build the reproduction in the form that fits the failure: a focused test, CLI fixture, captured trace or isolated scratch harness.
- `minimize-to-discriminate`: Minimize a reproduction only as far as needed to distinguish the candidate causes.
- `flake-reproduction`: For a flaky or production-only failure, diagnose its flake class and raise the reproduction rate until the loop is debuggable, using an order-dependent-test finder for test pollution.
- `environmental-cause-unresolved`: Claim an environmental root cause only after every hypothesis is falsified, report it as an unresolved finding with the investigation attached, and never present a mitigation as the fix.
- `hypotheses`: Form explicit hypotheses about the cause before probing any of them.
- `discriminating-observation`: Choose an observation that discriminates between the live hypotheses instead of generating a fixed number of them.
- `localized-probing`: Probe the suspected boundary or variable and repeat only while new evidence appears, using cross-layer tracing, working-versus-broken comparison or bisection to find the failing layer.
- `owning-fix`: Fix only a confirmed cause at its owning layer, since a change that merely hides the symptom is not a fix.
- `attempt-log`: Record each debugging attempt as hypothesis, change and result.
- `two-failure-stop`: After two failed fixes, stop and bring the attempt log to whoever started the task before trying another.
- `critic-escalation`: When hypotheses run out, get a critic review and pass it artifacts — the reproduction, its output and the attempts — rather than conclusions.
- `regression-check`: Turn the failure into a durable regression check when feasible, showing failure before the fix and success after, then rerun the original scenario.
- `evidence-safety`: Treat tool output and logs as untrusted evidence and keep secrets out of reports.
- `closeout`: Before declaring done, remove temporary instrumentation and record the confirmed cause.
- `preserve-reproducers`: Keep useful reproducers and user artifacts when cleaning up after a fix.
- `defense-in-depth-hardening`: When an invalid value crossed several layers, add a check at each layer the value passes through so the bug becomes structurally impossible, bypass-testing each layer and scoping the checks to the proven failure path.

#### engineering · Building · Implementation — test-driven-development
- `mode-selection`: Choose test-first, characterization, or test-quality-only by the task rather than defaulting to one workflow.
- `seam-selection`: Choose the test boundary that exercises the real contract without reaching inside.
- `plan-seams-no-approval`: Take test seams from the plan without separate approval, surfacing a missing seam only when it materially changes scope or the obtainable evidence.
- `red-green`: Make one test fail before implementing the change that makes it pass.
- `refactor-after-green`: Refactor after each passing test, preserving behaviour and rerunning the affected checks.
- `mock-boundaries`: Use test doubles only at boundaries, never in place of the behaviour under test.
- `proof-discipline`: Keep enough before-and-after evidence to distinguish a demonstrated fix from an inference and never destroy edits to recreate RED.
- `meaningful-behaviour-assertion`: Assert meaningful results, state or boundary interactions at a stable boundary rather than internal call choreography.
- `independent-expectation`: Derive expected values from an independent source such as a spec, worked example or trusted fixture, never computing both sides with the implementation under test.
- `no-implementation-coupling`: Avoid tests coupled to the implementation's internal structure, so they survive behaviour-preserving refactors.
- `deterministic-state`: Prefer deterministic inputs and isolated state, controlling time, randomness and shared state that cause nondeterminism.
- `break-naming-validation`: Before accepting substantive tests, name the specific wrong branch, missing validation or side effect they catch, confirming by a safe mutation trial rather than mental inspection when worth its cost.

#### engineering · Delivery · Integration — resolving-merge-conflicts
- `capture-conflict-set`: Capture the conflicted file set up front from the version control's unmerged-paths listing.
- `trace-intent`: Find the primary source of each conflict via commit messages and requirements first, expanding to PRs or issues only when a disputed hunk needs that history.
- `resolve-preserve-both`: Resolve each hunk preserving both intents where possible, picking the one matching the merge's stated goal where incompatible and noting the trade-off, inventing no new behaviour.
- `resolve-over-abort`: Resolve rather than reflexively aborting, stopping to ask the user before aborting when intents cannot reconcile or the operation itself is wrong.
- `run-project-checks`: Discover and run the project's automated checks and fix what the merge broke.
- `explicit-staging`: Stage only the resolved files from the captured conflict set by explicit path.
- `commit-authority-gate`: Commit or continue the rebase only with granted authority, otherwise stop with the resolution staged and report what would be committed.

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — codebase-design
- `module-vocabulary`: Reason about design with a shared deep-module glossary: module, interface, depth, seam, adapter and locality.
- `project-term-allowance`: Let the project's own precise terms, such as API, service or boundary, stand beside the design glossary rather than banning them.
- `interface-is-everything`: Treat an interface as every fact a caller must know — invariants, ordering, errors, configuration and performance — not just the type signature.
- `depth-as-leverage`: Prefer modules whose manageable interface hides a large amount of useful behaviour.
- `deletion-test`: Question a layer that only forwards and keep one whose removal would spread complexity across callers.
- `inject-dependencies`: Pass a module's external dependencies in as arguments rather than constructing them inside it, so callers and tests can substitute them.
- `return-not-mutate`: Design functions to return results rather than cause side effects, so behaviour can be observed directly.
- `single-adapter-justified`: Accept an interface justified by encapsulation, ownership or a present testing need with a single adapter, treating extra adapters as evidence of real variation rather than a prerequisite.
- `internal-seams`: Allow internal seams and focused internal tests without exposing internals through the public interface merely to satisfy a testing rule.
- `dependency-categories`: Classify a module's dependencies as in-process, locally substitutable, owned remote or true external to choose how it is tested across its seam.
- `covered-test-removal`: Remove an old test only when its behaviour is covered elsewhere or deliberately retired, inspecting a changed test rather than deleting it automatically.
- `design-it-twice`: Optionally compare a few materially different interface designs before a consequential choice, without forcing a multi-agent exercise on a clear one.

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — design-evolve
- `integration-not-redesign`: Integrate only authorized decisions into the next version and never treat integration as licence to redesign.
- `resolve-scope`: Resolve source version, target path and included discussion files from the request, using supplied paths without reconfirmation and asking only about missing scope or overwrite permission.
- `classify-maturity`: Inventory source and discussions by concept, separating authoritative decisions from proposals, scratchpads and unresolved conflicts.
- `evidence-before-edit`: Read the actual discussion and affected core sections before a consequential change and record a source-to-target change map, shown before a multi-concept edit.
- `start-from-source`: Begin each target from its complete source and preserve exact identifiers, numbers, error behaviour and invariants unless explicitly superseded.
- `no-gap-filling`: Never fill a gap the source leaves open; record it as TBD with its source and keep ambiguous choices unresolved.
- `version-rekey`: Update version headers, filenames and internal references and copy untouched core files so the target stands alone with prior versions only in provenance.
- `consistency-check`: Check cross-document consistency, section links, invariant coverage and stale version references, consolidating routine duplication but asking when consolidation changes meaning or authority.
- `concept-map`: Keep a compact concept map of source, maturity, affected sections, decision, exclusions and conflicts as an evidence artifact, with durable status in the tracker.
- `layout-mirror`: Mirror the source layout and filename convention under the target version, searching every form of the old version identifier rather than blind-replacing.
- `preserve-structure`: Preserve heading hierarchy, invariant identifiers, table meanings and link targets, distilling implementation guides into decisions only when their meaning is clear.
- `report-provenance`: Report integrated concepts, files, decisions and deferred items with source pointers, never labelling unresolved scratchpad proposals as approved design.

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — domain-modeling
- `active-discipline`: Actively build the model by challenging terms, inventing scenarios and writing it down, as distinct from merely reading the glossary.
- `declared-glossary-location`: Use the glossary location declared by project instructions, reusing an existing root glossary rather than creating a competing one.
- `lazy-glossary-and-adr`: Create glossary and decision-record files lazily, only when there is something concrete to write.
- `challenge-glossary`: Call out immediately a term that conflicts with the existing glossary language.
- `sharpen-fuzzy`: Propose one precise canonical term for a vague or overloaded one.
- `concrete-scenarios`: Stress-test domain relationships with invented edge-case scenarios that force precision about boundaries.
- `cross-reference-code`: Check whether the code agrees with a stated domain rule and surface contradictions.
- `update-inline`: Write a resolved term into the glossary as soon as it is resolved rather than batching changes.
- `authorized-model-writes`: Edit the glossary and decision records only when documentation work is authorized, otherwise reporting the proposed terms and decisions.
- `glossary-is-glossary`: Keep the glossary free of implementation details and never treat it as a spec or scratchpad.
- `glossary-format`: Write opinionated glossary entries with an Avoid list and tight is-not-does definitions, grouped under subheadings when clusters emerge.
- `context-specific-terms`: Admit only terms specific to the project's context to the glossary, leaving general programming concepts out.
- `multi-context-map`: Maintain a root context map listing contexts, their locations and relationships, inferring which context a topic belongs to or asking.
- `adr-three-gate`: Offer a decision record only when the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.
- `adr-minimal-template`: Use a one-paragraph decision record with optional status, options and consequences and sequential numbering.
- `adr-what-qualifies`: Apply a worked list of decision kinds (architectural shape, integration patterns, lock-in choices, boundaries, deliberate deviations, hidden constraints, non-obvious rejections) that warrant a decision record.
- `adr-match-convention`: Match an existing decision-record convention (location, extension, numbering, headings) before applying defaults, surfacing conflicts instead of adding a second scheme.
- `adr-supersede-lifecycle`: Never delete a decision record; supersede it with a new one and mark the old one superseded.
- `adr-code-gotcha-link`: Leave a short comment at a code trap or constraint linking the decision record that explains it.

#### engineering · Design · Architecture — prototype
- `named-question`: Build a throwaway artifact to answer one named design question.
- `pick-form`: Let the question being answered pick the prototype's form, such as a state demo for logic or a UI mockup for layout.
- `throwaway-marked`: Keep prototypes clearly marked as throwaway and separate from production.
- `trivial-to-run`: Make the prototype trivial to run: one command, or a single HTML file the user opens directly.
- `surface-state`: Surface the relevant state and the invalid transitions the design might mishandle.
- `scoped-data`: Use synthetic or appropriately scoped data, bringing in external calls and real integration only when the question needs them and they are authorized.
- `persistence-when-needed`: Bring persistence into a prototype only when the question needs it.
- `cheap-assertions`: Use a small assertion as the cheapest proof where it helps, since a prototype implies neither a full test suite nor a ban on checks.
- `logic-pure-module`: Keep domain logic readable apart from presentation as a reducer, state machine, pure functions or small stateful module.
- `logic-shareable-html`: Offer a self-contained HTML demo with the question, a readable state panel, controls and guided scenarios that reset to a known state.
- `ui-contextual-preview`: Prefer an isolated preview, or an authorized existing-page preview that cannot leak into production, over a new live route.
- `variants-when-comparing`: Build UI variants only when comparing alternatives is the question the prototype answers.
- `structural-variants`: Make UI variants differ in meaningful structure and layout, not just colour or styling.
- `variant-switcher`: Provide a labelled control for switching between UI variants.
- `ui-keyboard-safety`: Keep a prototype's keyboard shortcuts from intercepting input while an editable field is focused.
- `ui-accessibility`: Keep focus, contrast and interaction states usable in a UI prototype while real mutations are stubbed.
- `capture-outcome`: Record the prototype's verdict and the question it settled, with a pointer to the preserved artifact.
- `separate-promotion`: Treat promoting a prototype's decision or code into production as separate work with its own scope and checks.

#### engineering · Design · Decomposition — planning
- `route-by-scale`: Route between brainstorming, a brief local sequence, elaborate, decompose, or executing from a roadmap row according to the work's scale.
- `decompose-phases`: Split an approved spec into demoable phases with checkable exits and flat stages that each carry acceptance.
- `vertical-slices`: Prefer independently verifiable vertical slices over horizontal layers.
- `expand-contract`: For a broad refactor use expand, migrate then contract with genuine dependencies, naming one integration boundary when intermediate tasks cannot stay green.
- `dependency-edges`: Encode real blocking edges in the tracker and let the ready frontier drive execution rather than listing order.
- `beads-native-tracking`: Seed epics and stages and render tracking natively in the tracker, keeping the roadmap anchor on the epics and the stage mapping that execution closes against, and writing nothing before its matching approval.
- `durable-plan-format`: Produce a durable plan with ownership boundaries, interfaces, verification, dependencies and known files, saved to the plans path and approval-gated.
- `plan-evidence-bound`: List known files but do not invent exact symbols or freeze a file map without evidence, leaving implementers to discover internals within their ownership.
- `test-first-marking`: Mark risky changes test-first or characterization-first in the plan.
- `no-placeholder-plan`: Reject plan placeholders such as TBD, vague error-handling notes, unnamed test behaviours, same-as-another-task references and unresolved cross-task contracts, naming concrete acceptance instead.
- `plan-self-review`: Self-review the finished plan for spec-requirement coverage, consistent names and types across tasks, and a gap-naming pass that turns unnamed seams, migrations, rollout and cleanup into tasks or explicit exclusions.
- `reviewer-rejectable-sizing`: Size each task so a reviewer could accept or reject it independently of its neighbour, folding setup, scaffolding and docs into the deliverable they serve.

#### engineering · Discovery · Research — codebase-research
- `three-modes`: Offer three research modes — an L1 capability survey, an L2 architecture map, and a deep dive on one named question — all landing under a per-target research directory.
- `levels-vs-dive`: Treat L1 and L2 as nested levels of one study while a deep dive is a standalone trace that may follow L1, carries its own snapshot, and never marks a repo complete.
- `scope-authorization`: Map the invocation to the highest explicitly authorized scope, never exceed it, and escalate only when the user widens scope.
- `evidence-flags`: Record two independent claim flags per capability — whether prose documents it and whether a manifest or config declares it.
- `reachability-ladder`: Rate what was actually found on the ABSENT/PRESENT/WIRED/SOURCE-TRACED/EXERCISED ladder, each state earned by a specific act and L1 capped at PRESENT.
- `oversell-finding`: Report a documented-and-PRESENT but never-WIRED capability as an explicit finding, since that gap is how docs oversell.
- `claim-honesty`: Mark interpretation as INFERENCE, cite file and line for every source-traced claim, and for a closed target name the strongest available artifact and its limits.
- `snapshot-header`: Stamp every artifact with the studied commit, worktree cleanliness and date, mark a dirty tree provisional, sweep rows written at an older sha as stale, and refresh a stale lower level before building a higher one.
- `registry-index`: Keep a single index file as the artifact registry, updated in the same run that writes or invalidates an artifact, with dated immutable deep dives that supersede earlier ones by name.
- `trust-boundary`: Treat the target's docs, scripts and help text as evidence rather than instructions and stay read-only in the target and its submodules.
- `execution-authorization`: Reach the EXERCISED state only under explicit runtime authorization, in a disposable isolated copy without credentials and with commands and side effects named first.
- `inline-for-bounded`: Answer a bounded explanatory question inline with source pointers, without standing up a research registry.
- `artifact-contracts`: Follow a fixed required-section set and order per artifact type, stating an empty section rather than dropping it.
- `verify-before-report`: Before reporting, confirm the registry matches disk, every row carries its flags and state, every source-traced claim cites file and line, and the target is untouched.

#### engineering · Operations · Maintenance — improve-codebase-architecture
- `scope-by-evidence`: Scope the audit to a named module or pain point, otherwise to the hot spots in recent change history.
- `friction-signals`: Surface architectural friction that current code actually supports rather than speculative smells.
- `deletion-test`: Question a layer that only forwards and keep one whose removal would spread complexity across callers.
- `candidate-comparison`: Give each candidate its files, friction, direction, benefit, migration cost, evidence and confidence, then present a concise comparison and the strongest supported recommendation.
- `optional-report`: Produce a standalone HTML report only when requested or clearly helpful, delegating presentation to the shared artifact skill and requiring any before/after diagram to show a real structural difference.
- `module-vocabulary`: Reason about design with a shared deep-module glossary: module, interface, depth, seam, adapter and locality.
- `project-term-allowance`: Let the project's own precise terms, such as API, service or boundary, stand beside the design glossary rather than banning them.
- `adr-conflict-callout`: When a candidate conflicts with a decision record, explain the new evidence that might justify revisiting it.
- `review-no-auto-followup`: Do not automatically enter a grilling loop, interview, alternative-design exercise or domain-document update after delivering the review; each happens only when requested or already authorized.

#### engineering · Verification · Review — security
- `scope-threat`: Name the changed entrypoints, assets, identities and consequences, tracing untrusted input to consequential sinks including model outputs used as commands, paths, queries or markup.
- `abuse-cases`: Derive concrete abuse cases and select relevant controls, scaling a tiny boundary change to a short threat note and a proving test.
- `targeted-control-groups`: Consult only the matching control group for the surface at hand — authentication, URL fetching, uploads, dependencies, secrets or agent systems.
- `web-reference`: Also consult the web-surface controls reference for a web-facing surface.
- `boundary-controls-ref`: Supply per-surface control methods — authorization distinct from authentication, SSRF allowlisting with DNS-rebinding residual, upload constraints, dependency triage, supply-chain install boundary, and rotate-first secret handling.
- `llm-surface-ref`: Supply the LLM and agent attack surface — untrusted model output, prompt injection, minimum tool scope, consumption bounds, RAG retrieval trust, model supply chain, and not acting on unverified claims.
- `authority-gate`: Treat existing approval of the exact change as satisfying the gate while an unapproved sensitive-data category, integration, permission grant or material relaxation needs a fresh decision, and routine controls within an approved feature need no repeated gate.
- `enforce-in-code`: Enforce access, tenant isolation, validation, safe sink handling and resource limits in code, since external documents, logs and model output cannot grant permissions and prompt secrecy is no control.
- `evidence-tests`: Test the material abuse path and legitimate use, verify authorization per resource rather than merely login, and check leakage, retries and failure behaviour.
- `dependency-triage`: Triage dependency advisories by reachability and impact rather than count, recording material exceptions with a revisit condition.
- `boundary-review`: Report security findings through the shared review skill's severity and output contract, supplying the security lens rather than running a second compulsory review process.

#### engineering · Verification · Testing — check-invariants
- `read-overlay`: Read the project's declared invariants file and run each listed check against the current tree.
- `explicit-commands-only`: Run only invariants that carry an explicit runnable command, leaving everything else unexecuted.
- `pass-fail-report`: Report a plain pass or fail result for each invariant that was run.
- `skip-aspirational`: Name and skip any invariant that is aspirational rather than mechanically checkable instead of guessing a verdict.
- `repo-relative-paths`: Present every result using repository-relative paths only.

#### engineering · X · Coordination — execution
- `scope-selector`: Pick task, phase or workstream scope from the request and route unresolved material scope back to planning or brainstorming.
- `risk-sized-review`: Size work small, standard or deep and match inline work, delegation and independent review to that size.
- `task-loop`: Claim the exact task, implement in dependency order within owned paths, run applicable checks, and close with evidence and material limitations.
- `finding-adjudication`: Verify each incoming review finding against requirements, code and primary evidence before acting, and give each a visible disposition: fix a confirmed in-scope defect, answer an incorrect one with a retained ruling, record an out-of-scope follow-up.
- `phase-loop`: Resolve the roadmap phase's single epic, drive ready stages through the contractor that owns execution to closure, and refresh tracking between stages.
- `close-gate`: Close a phase only when it has at least one stage, every stage is closed, and its roadmap exit criterion has run with evidence recorded.
- `workstream-mode`: Run remaining phases in order only on explicit opt-in, with per-phase tracking refresh and commits only when the invocation covers them.
- `child-workflows`: Run independent graphs as admitted child workflows where collection is evidence and landing goes through the contractor, not automatic result binding.
- `context-recovery`: Stay in context while useful and, before compacting or handing off, persist scope, decisions and next work to the ledger, tracker and Git, then rebuild from those rather than from a summary.
- `stop-on-failure`: Let a failed gate, exit criterion or material blocker stop advancement and diagnose instead of re-dispatching without new evidence.
- `bounded-fix-loop`: Group compatible confirmed findings into one fix unit, re-review only the delta plus any breakage it caused, adjudicate every round, and treat a small fixed count of completed fix/re-review rounds as a ceiling rather than a target.
- `scope-base-review-package`: Review uncommitted working-tree and untracked changes against a recorded base revision by passing the authorized owned-path list, never attributing a baseline-dirty file's whole diff to the task.
- `delegated-report-recovery`: Interpret each delegated worker's status (done, done-with-concerns, needs-context, blocked) and recover by supplying context, splitting, debugging or replanning, since bare repetition is not recovery.

### mattpocock_skills

#### core · Discovery · Charting — skill:skills/engineering/wayfinder
- `decision-map-epic`: Chart a large effort as one map item on the tracker whose children are decision tickets.
- `plan-not-do`: Keep the map to planning: each ticket resolves a decision rather than executing a build slice.
- `reference-by-name`: Reference tickets by name with identifiers and links so the map reads without opening every item.
- `map-as-index`: Keep resolution detail on each ticket while the map holds only a named pointer and a gist.
- `map-body-sections`: Structure the map body as Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, and Out of scope.
- `bounded-decision-ticket`: Make each ticket one bounded question whose answer is a decision.
- `session-sized-tickets`: Size each ticket to fit one agent session's context window.
- `claim-before-work`: Choose the requested or a ready unclaimed child and claim it before working on it.
- `dependency-edges`: Encode real blocking edges in the tracker and let the ready frontier drive execution rather than listing order.
- `ticket-type-set`: A fixed set of ticket kinds: research for facts, prototype for fidelity, grilling for a live interview, and task for prerequisite work that unblocks a decision.
- `live-human-resolution`: Resolve a human-in-the-loop item only through a live exchange with the human, never answering the human's side yourself.
- `question-graduation`: Ticket a question once it is sharp enough to state, even while blocked, and hold not-yet-specifiable work aside until earlier answers make it expressible.
- `out-of-scope-close`: Close an out-of-scope ticket with an explicit exclusion reason rather than a claim of delivery.
- `one-ticket-per-session`: Resolve no more than one ticket per session, except research tickets.
- `research-subagent-branch`: Resolve research tickets with subagents that capture findings on a throwaway research branch.
- `real-id-wiring`: Wire cross-references and dependencies with real identifiers, never placeholders.
- `no-triage-labels`: Carry only wayfinder-type labels on a map and its tickets, never a triage label.
- `research-branch-pr-policy`: Push the research branch but open no pull request from it, and never merge it.
- `type-directed-resolution`: Resolve each ticket as the type its label names, reading the label rather than inferring from the body.
- `destination-first`: Name the destination first, since it fixes the scope and shapes every ticket.
- `no-map-without-fog`: If breadth-first charting surfaces no fog, stop and ask how to proceed rather than building a map.
- `record-resolution`: On resolving a ticket, record the answer on it, close it, and add a pointer to the map's decisions so far.

#### core · Discovery · Research — skill:skills/engineering/research
- `background-agent`: Delegate reading legwork to a background agent so the caller keeps working while it investigates.
- `primary-source-preference`: Prefer primary sources such as official docs, source code and specs over secondary write-ups.
- `cited-artifact`: Bind citations to the claims they support in the research output.
- `findings-file`: Always write the findings to one Markdown file saved where the repository keeps such notes.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:skills/engineering/grill-with-docs
- `document-during-interview`: Pair a clarifying interview with live documentation so the glossary and decision records are produced as the interview settles each question.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:skills/in-progress/loop-me
- `loop-lens`: See the user's life as loops within loops to find recurring activities worth delegating, proposing ones they have not noticed.
- `workflow-spec-artifact`: Keep each workflow's spec in its own markdown file as the single source of truth.
- `spec-done-when-buildable`: Treat a spec as done only when an implementer could build it without asking a single question.
- `world-notes`: Capture the user's world, tools, channels and terminology in a notes file, interviewing them first when it is thin.
- `workflow-vocabulary`: Describe a workflow with a shared vocabulary of Trigger, an event or schedule, and Checkpoint.
- `mandate-nothing-structural`: Impose no structure such as AI, a checkpoint or a schedule on a workflow unless the interview shows it is needed.
- `push-right`: Defer the human checkpoint as far as it will go, doing maximal work first so the human is asked once, late, with everything prepared.
- `decision-summary-brief`: Present a checkpoint as a tight, decision-ready summary of what was produced and why with a link, never the raw output.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:skills/productivity/grilling
- `map-decisions`: Map the material decisions and their prerequisites before questioning.
- `question-batching`: Batch independent questions whose prerequisites are settled and defer each dependent question until its prerequisites are answered.
- `recommended-answer`: Attach a recommended answer to each question, letting the respondent disagree.
- `yes-accepts-recommendation`: Word each question so that a yes accepts your recommended answer.
- `round-format`: Lay out each round in a fixed question-and-recommendation markdown format, one block per question.
- `self-serve-facts`: Look up available facts yourself rather than asking, leaving only the decisions to the live participant.
- `exhaustive-completion`: End the session only when the frontier is empty and every branch of the tree has been visited, with nothing silently assumed.
- `reconfirm-before-action`: Do not act until the user confirms a shared understanding has been reached.

#### core · Intake · Clarification — skill:skills/productivity/to-questionnaire
- `grill-the-send`: Ask the present user only about the send (who it goes to and what they need back), never about the subject the recipient knows.
- `two-exchange-interview`: Run the interview as two bounded exchanges, the recipient and what the user needs back.
- `gap-targeted-questions`: Aim a questionnaire's questions at the gap between what the recipient knows and what the sender needs.
- `questionnaire-artifact`: Write the questionnaire to a slug-named markdown file in the current directory and report its path.
- `document-structure`: Fill a fixed questionnaire template, ordered most-important-first, of purpose, from/to/use, context, how-to-answer, themed sections of one-idea questions with answer stubs, and a closing catch-all.

#### core · Improvement · Codification — skill:skills/productivity/writing-for-agents
- `context-pointers`: Write a pointer that names the material and the condition for reaching it, front-loading the trigger.
- `two-loads`: Weigh always-loaded context cost on the agent against cognitive load on the human.
- `inline-vs-disclose`: Inline what every branch needs and disclose branch-specific material behind a conditional pointer.
- `co-location`: Keep a concept's definition, rules and caveats under one heading so reading one part brings its neighbours.
- `completion-criteria-clarity`: End each step on an observable, checkable done-or-not-done criterion that resists premature completion.
- `completion-criteria-demand`: Phrase the criterion to demand thorough work, driving the legwork latent in its wording.
- `split-by-invocation`: Split off a model-invoked skill only when a distinct leading word should trigger it or another skill must reach it.
- `sequence-isolation`: Split a run of steps so later post-completion steps stay out of view, driving more legwork on the step in front.
- `leading-words`: Anchor behaviour in a compact pretrained concept repeated as a token, reaching for an existing word before coining one.
- `negation-avoidance`: Steer by the positive target because negation makes the forbidden behaviour more available, keeping prohibitions a last-resort guardrail.
- `single-source-of-truth`: Keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing it is a one-place edit.
- `environment-as-cache`: Point to authoritative commands and lookups instead of copying volatile facts the agent can find itself.
- `relevance-check`: Check every line still bears on the document's task, pruning stale or irrelevant ones.
- `no-op-deletion`: Delete instructions the model already follows by default.
- `invocation-mode`: Choose model-invoked or user-invoked activation, setting the disable-model-invocation flag for manual workflows.
- `shared-reference-home`: Put reference several skills need in one model-invoked, all-reference skill they can each invoke.
- `router-skills`: When user-invoked skills multiply, add a user-invoked router skill that names the others and when to reach each, hinting rather than firing them.

#### core · X · Communication — skill:skills/productivity/wait-what
- `repitch-trigger`: When a message did not land, stop and re-pitch it rather than adding more.
- `controlled-language`: Re-pitch in controlled simplified language with short sentences and common words.
- `domain-vocabulary`: Use the project's established domain vocabulary throughout what you write.
- `context-map-lookup`: Follow the context map to the right context's glossary when the repository has several.

#### core · X · Continuity — skill:skills/productivity/handoff
- `handoff-doc`: Write a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work.
- `temp-dir-destination`: Save the handoff to the operating system's temporary directory rather than the workspace.
- `suggested-skills`: Name in the handoff which skills the next agent should reach for.
- `link-dont-copy`: Reference existing artifacts by path or URL rather than copying their content into a handoff.
- `redact-secrets`: Redact secrets and personal data as placeholders in anything shown or saved, driving commands from environment variables so credentials never appear.
- `tailor-to-next-focus`: Treat any passed arguments as the next session's focus and tailor the handoff to it.

#### core · U · Tutoring — skill:skills/productivity/teach
- `teaching-workspace`: Keep a multi-session course's state (mission, resources, learning records, glossary and lessons) as files in one course workspace.
- `always-stateful-course`: Treat every teaching request as a stateful multi-session course kept in the workspace.
- `workspace-from-run-dir`: Resolve workspace paths from the directory the skill was run in, resolving only the format-template links from the skill folder.
- `mission-grounding`: A mission document capturing the concrete real-world reason for learning that anchors every teaching choice.
- `proximal-next-lesson`: When the learner names no target, choose the next lesson from the learning records and mission so it challenges them just enough.
- `storage-strength`: Favour long-term retention over in-the-moment fluency, which can give an illusory sense of mastery.
- `retrieval-practice`: Have the learner retrieve answers from memory through exercises or questions.
- `spacing`: Space practice over time to build long-term retention.
- `interleaving`: Interleave different but related topics in practice.
- `lesson-format`: Make each lesson short and self-contained, teaching one tightly scoped objective tied to the learner's goal.
- `html-lessons`: Deliver every lesson as one self-contained HTML file.
- `reusable-assets`: Reuse existing lesson assets before creating new ones.
- `shared-component-extraction`: Write each new reusable lesson piece as a shared component and link to it, never inlining code a later lesson would duplicate.
